title: Controllable and Content Based Recommendations
claim: A multi-stage pipeline turns raw content into text profiles, then aligns them with a frozen collaborative-filtering model to produce recommendations.
layout: 3 numbered stages, left-to-right, dashed dividers, module labels beneath each stage
description: A wide, three-stage figure with numbered blue circles and bold titles: (1) Content-Based Profile Construction, (2) Profile-Tag Alignment, (3) Collaborative Filtering Alignment. Dashed vertical lines separate the stages. Stage 1 starts with audio, image and video icons. They feed a content dataset cylinder, then a green multimodal language model. That model produces dashed item-description boxes, which a green large language model turns into a user profile box with avatars. Stage 2 has an orange language embedder trapezoid, a linear layer, a tag distribution plot and the tag-alignment loss. Stage 3 has a blue frozen CF encoder, a linear projection, an orange CF decoder, interaction boxes, a final-objectives box and final recommendations. Hollow arrows show the flow, with loss formulas next to them. Pastel green, orange and blue distinguish module types. The eye goes first to the left-hand icons.
caption: Overview of the CCBR pipeline. 1) Item-level content (images, audio, or video) is first verbalized into natural-language descriptions by a multimodal language model, and a language model then aggregates each user's interacted items into a textual preference profile. 2) The profile is mapped to a dense representation through a trainable text encoder and a linear projection head. 3) This text-side representation is aligned with the user representation produced by a frozen collaborative filtering backbone, whose decoder is reused to score candidate items.
abstract: Traditional recommendation systems rely on latent (dense) representations, making them difficult to interpret and control. We propose the Controllable and Content-Based Recommendations (CCBR) framework, which builds its recommendations from textual user profile representations. CCBR plugs into collaborative filtering models and introduces controllability via text bottlenecks. We show that CCBR enables text-based and multimodal interventions, allowing users to steer the model towards the directions they prefer. Different from existing controllable recommendation systems, CCBR infers the text summaries directly from item contents (images, audio or video). Across image, audio, and video datasets, we demonstrate that the proposed framework obtains competitive model performance with standard (latent-representation) models while providing controllable model summaries via text. The model also outperforms TEARS, a recent baseline for controllable recommendation systems. Through systematic interventions, we demonstrate the efficacy of the steering mechanism.
